details:
Project Details

The Earth's Lullaby is an interactive web experience that transforms NASA's night time-light visualizations into an ambient musical soundscape. Developed by Team Centauri for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, The Earth information Jukebox, the project offers an alternative way to explore Earth's night-time patterns through both sight and sound.

How does it work ?

The experience uses NASA's Black Marble annual night time-light visualizations from the years 2012 to 2023, based on Suomi NPP VIIRS satellite observations. Users can select a year through an interactive timeline, view its corresponding global map and listen to a generated soundscape. We process the rendered visualization images using Python and Pillow to estimate relative visual brightness. These estimates influence musical pitch and harmony through the Web Audio API, creating a gentle five-second sound sequence for each year. Users can navigate between years, play or pause the experience and control the sound.

Benefits and intended impacts

The project introduces a creative way to engage with Earth Science information by adding an auditory dimension to satellite visualizations. It encourages curiosity about night-time light patterns, supports exploratory learning and demonstrates how open space-based data can be transformed into interactive experiences. Our intention is to make Earth observation more engaging and memorable for people who may not normally interact with satellite imagery.

Tools and technologies used

  • Frontend : Next.js, React and Typescript
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS
  • Image processing: Python and Pillow
  • Audio generation: Web Audio API
  • Data Visualization: NASA Black marble annual image frames
  • Version control: Git and Github
  • Deployment: Vercel

Creativity and Innovation

Our creative approach lies in translating visual data into sound. Rather than presenting the night-lights map

as static images, we use estimated brightness patterns to influence musical tones and harmonies. The result is an experience where users can listen to a visual interpretation of Earth's night time lights, turning satellite imagery into an ambient journey.

Factors Considered

During development, we considered scientific transparency, accessibility, usability, performance and visual presentation. Since our brightness estimates are calculated from rendered visualization images rather than raw calibrated satellite radiance, we clearly communicate this limitation. We also optimized the original TIFF images into WebP formats for faster loading, designed simple playback controls, maintained a consistent five-second audio duration per year and created a responsive interface for different screen sizes.

The Earth's lullaby is ultimately an exploration of how scientific data, technology and creativity can come together to help people experience our planet in a new way.
